Whether PORT can benefit patients with surgically resected NSCLC has been the topic of decades of clinical research. The PORT meta-analysis, published in 1998 and including trials published as early as 1980, showed an adverse effect of PORT on survival, except in N2 (ipsilateral mediastinal nodal) disease where there wasno clear evidence of an adverse effect.

Because the data in the case of N2 disease were equivocal and given ongoing technological improvements in the delivery of radiotherapy (RT), investig ators sought evidence that PORT is beneficial in the case of N2 disease. Benefits vs. risks of traditional PORT
In the Lung ART trial, those in the PORT group had substantially fewer mediastinal relapses (25%) compared to those in the control group (46%), and so one would anticipate a DFS benefit.

However, there was substantially higher late grade 3-4 cardiopulmonarytoxicity in the PORT group (11%) vs. control group (5%), and there were 16 deaths due to cardiopulmonary disease in the PORT group vs. 2 in the control group. Importantly to note, the volumes treated in the

arms.label: Arm I
arms.text: Patients in arm I receive intrathecal cytarabine in week 1; infusions of vincristine and daunorubicin once a week in weeks 1-4; dexamethasone by mouth or infusion twice a day in weeks 1 and 2; intrathecal methotrexate in weeks 2 and 5 or 2-5; and an injection of pegaspargase in week 1.

arms.label: Arm II
arms.text: Patients in arm II will receive intrathecal cytarabine in week 1; infusions of vincristine and daunorubicin once a week in weeks 1-4; dexamethasone by mouth or infusion twice a day in weeks 1 and 2; intrathecal methotrexate in weeks 2 and 5 or 2-5; and an injection of pegaspargase in week 1.

arms.label: Arm III
arms.text: Patients in arm III will receive cytarabine, vincristine, daunorubicin, and pegaspargase as in groups one and two. They will also receive prednisone by mouth or infusion twice a day in weeks 1-4 and intrathecal methotrexate in weeks 2 and 5. Some patients in all groups may receive induction therapy for 2 additional weeks. Beginning in week 6 or 7, patients may receive combination chemotherapy by infusion, injection, intrathecally, and by mouth for up to 8 weeks.

arms.label: Arm IV
arms.text: Patients in arm IV will receive cytarabine, vincristine, daunorubicin, and pegaspargase as in groups one and two. They will also receive prednisone by mouth or infusion twice a day in weeks 1-4 and intrathecal methotrexate in weeks 2 and 5. Some patients in all groups may receive induction therapy for 2 additional weeks. Beginning in week 6 or 7, patients may receive combination chemotherapy by infusion, injection, intrathecally, and by mouth for up to 8 weeks.

schema.label: Disease
schema.text: cT2-cT3N0 muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma of the bladder.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Clinical stage T2 vs T3. Planned radiosensitizer: cisplatin, gemcitabine, or mitomycin-C/5-FU. Neoadjuvant therapy yes vs no.

schema.label: Randomize 1:1
schema.text: Protocol treatment starts within 28 days after randomization. Arm 2 must use plan-of-the-day or online adaptive radiotherapy.

arms.label: Arm 1
arms.text: 4 weeks of radiosensitizing chemotherapy plus hypofractionated radiotherapy, 55 Gy in 20 fractions.

arms.label: Arm 2
arms.text: 4 weeks of radiosensitizing chemotherapy plus SBRT, 32.5 Gy in 5 fractions.

schema.note: Radiosensitizing chemotherapy is limited to the 4-week window. Missed or held doses are not made up.

schema.label: Primary question
schema.text: Non-inferiority of ultra-hypofractionation versus hypofractionation for 3-year bladder-intact event-free survival. The margin is 10% (50% to 40%), corresponding to a hazard ratio below 1.32.

eligibility: Histologic cT2-T3N0M0 urothelial carcinoma. Mixed urothelial carcinoma is allowed. Small cell carcinoma is not.
One TURBT before randomization. Maximal resection is attempted. Complete or partial resection are both allowed. A repeat TURBT after the initial TURBT is not required.
The window from TURBT pathology to randomization is 180 days. It extends to 240 days only when the patient has completed at least 3 cycles of neoadjuvant chemotherapy.

Staging of chest, abdomen, and pelvis with CT or MRI, or FDG PET, before randomization. No T4, node-positive, or metastatic disease. A node of 1.0 cm or larger in short axis requires a biopsy showing no tumor.
No diffuse CIS on cystoscopy and biopsy. No prior pelvic radiation. No urothelial carcinoma outside the bladder within 24 months, except upper-tract Ta, T1, or CIS after complete nephroureterectomy.
Age 18 or older. Zubrod performance status 0-2.

pretreatment.note: Extended to at most 240 days before randomization only after at least 3 cycles of neoadjuvant chemotherapy. A repeat TURBT is not required.
CT of chest, abdomen, and pelvis, or CT of chest and abdomen plus MRI of the pelvis, or FDG PET-CT.
Persons of childbearing potential.

submission.text: TRIAD is the NRG image exchange. It anonymizes and validates DICOM and other objects as they transfer.

submission.label: Arm 1, non-adaptive
submission.text: Submit the DICOM CT, planning MR when used, RT structure, RT dose for all initial plans, and RT plan for all initial plans. The first Arm 1 case from each site needs pre-treatment review before RT starts, unless that case uses adaptive planning, in which case the adaptive tables apply. After the site completes the required pre-treatment reviews, later Arm 1 submissions are due within 7 days of RT start.

submission.label: Plan library
submission.text: Required for Arm 2 and optional for Arm 1. The first Arm 2 plan-library case from each site needs pre-treatment review before RT, and a second pre-treatment review of delivered adapted fraction 1 before fraction 2. After those reviews, later cases are due within 7 days of the RT end date. The initial submission is the planning CT (three sets if differential bladder filling is used), planning MR when used, RT structures, three RT plans, and three RT doses. The delivered-fraction submission adds the selected plan and dose, daily volumetric images with alignment, a post-adaptation pre-delivery image, and a post-delivery image.

submission.label: Online adaptive
submission.text: Required for Arm 2. The first Arm 2 online-adaptive case from each site needs pre-treatment review before RT, and a second review of delivered adapted fraction 1 before fraction 2. After the site completes the required pre-treatment reviews, adaptive data for later Arm 2 cases are due within 14 days of the RT end date.

amendments.text: Protocol version date on the file. CTSU posted this version on September 8, 2026. The PDF has no document history and no section-level summary of what changed.

schema.label: Muscle-invasive disease
schema.text: Histologic cT2-T4aN0 urothelial carcinoma of the bladder.

schema.label: Neoadjuvant therapy
schema.text: Physician's choice, limited to the FDA-approved regimens in the eligibility criteria.

schema.label: Response assessment
schema.text: cT0 or cT1 on a repeat TURBT with systematic biopsies. That TURBT is within 90 days before registration.

schema.label: Registration
schema.text: Within 90 days after the last neoadjuvant dose.

schema.label: Treatment
schema.text: Bladder radiotherapy plus pembrolizumab for 1 year. Central radiation-plan approval is required before treatment starts. Radiotherapy is whole bladder only, 55 Gy in 20 fractions of 2.75 Gy, with no pelvic nodes and no tumor boost.

schema.label: On-study assessment
schema.text: Cystoscopy, cytology, and imaging.

schema.label: Endpoint
schema.text: 3-year bladder-intact event-free survival. Follow-up continues for 5 years after registration.

eligibility: Histologic cT2-T4aN0M0 muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma of the bladder within 180 days before neoadjuvant therapy starts. Staging CT, MRI, or PET of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis within 60 days before neoadjuvant therapy.

After neoadjuvant therapy, a repeat TURBT must show cT0 or cT1. It biopsies the prior disease and systematic sites (left and right lateral walls, dome, posterior wall, and trigone), with at least 4 of 5 systematic biopsies. The TURBT is within 60 days after the last neoadjuvant dose and within 90 days before registration.

No cT2 or higher, N1-3, or M1 disease after neoadjuvant therapy. A node of 1.0 cm or larger in short axis after neoadjuvant therapy needs PET-CT within 70 days before registration. A PET-positive node is ineligible unless biopsy shows no tumor.

At least 3 and no more than 6 cycles of FDA-approved neoadjuvant therapy: cisplatin-based combination chemotherapy, with or without a PD-1/L1 inhibitor; dose-dense or accelerated MVAC; or enfortumab vedotin with a PD-1/L1 inhibitor.
No small cell, neuroendocrine, or plasmacytoid histology. Mixed histology is allowed when more than half of the tumor is urothelial carcinoma. No prior pelvic radiotherapy.
The primary objective is written for clinically T0 or T1 disease without multifocal CIS. That CIS phrase is not an eligibility criterion.

pretreatment.window: Within 180 days before neoadjuvant therapy starts
pretreatment.note: Confirms muscle-invasive disease before systemic therapy.

pretreatment.item: Staging CT, MRI, or PET of chest, abdomen, and pelvis
pretreatment.note: Sets the pre-treatment stage.

pretreatment.window: Within 60 days after the last neoadjuvant dose, and within 90 days before registration
pretreatment.note: Must show cT0 or cT1. At least 4 of 5 systematic sites, plus the areas of prior disease.

pretreatment.item: Restaging chest, abdomen, and pelvis imaging
pretreatment.window: Within 60 days after the last neoadjuvant dose
pretreatment.note: CT or MRI, contrast preferred, or FDG PET-CT.

pretreatment.item: PET-CT for a node 1.0 cm or larger after neoadjuvant therapy
pretreatment.note: A PET-positive node requires a biopsy showing no tumor.

pretreatment.item: History and physical, CBC, chemistry, creatinine
pretreatment.note: The study calendar places these in the pre-registration column.

pretreatment.window: Within 90 days after the last neoadjuvant dose
pretreatment.note: Pembrolizumab is planned within 28 days after registration. Radiotherapy starts within 7 days of pembrolizumab and within 35 days after registration.

during.note: A visit already done within 28 days of cycle 1 day 1 does not need to be repeated.

during.window: Cycle 1 and cycles 2-18, within 3 days of each pembrolizumab infusion
during.note: During radiotherapy, labs follow institutional practice.
Planned to start within 28 days after registration.

during.window: Starts within 7 days of pembrolizumab and within 35 days after registration
during.note: Central plan approval is required before treatment.

followup.item: Disease assessment: CT, MRI, or PET; cystoscopy; urine cytology
followup.window: Every 12 weeks starting at 21 weeks, until 2 years, then every 26 weeks until 3 years

submission.label: TRIAD
submission.text: Digital RT data go to IROC through TRIAD. The submission is DICOM RT and must include the planning CT, structures, plan, and dose. sFTP to IROC Rhode Island is allowed when needed.

submission.label: Pre-treatment review
submission.text: Required for the first case of each modality, 3DCRT or IMRT, from each institution. IROC review must be received before RT starts for that first case. The review takes 3 business days.

submission.label: After radiotherapy
submission.text: Within 7 days after RT, the first case of each modality submits the RT treatment summary through TRIAD. Every later case submits the digital plan for the whole course and the RT treatment summary through TRIAD.

submission.label: Rave
submission.text: Within 30 days after each pembrolizumab cycle: vital status, treatment, and adverse event forms. Within 30 days after RT: vital status and the RT treatment summary. Within 30 days after each disease assessment while on protocol treatment: vital status, disease assessment, and the radiographic form if CT or MRI shows metastatic disease. Cytology reports are uploaded in Rave.

registry_schema.text: ClinicalTrials.gov arm list. This is not a protocol schema.

arms.label: Interventional: 6 R-CHOP-21
arms.text: Arm I (R-CHOP-21): Patients receive R-CHOP immunochemotherapy comprising rituximab IV, cyclophosphamide IV over 15 minutes, doxorubicin IV, and vincristine IV on day 1 and oral prednisone once daily on days 1-5. Treatment repeats every 21 days for up to 6 courses in the absence of disease progression or unacceptable toxicity.

arms.label: Interventional: 6 R-CHOP-21 + radiotherapy
arms.text: Arm II (R-CHOP-21 and radiotherapy): Patients receive R-CHOP as in arm I. Treatment repeats every 21 days for up to 6 courses in the absence of disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. Beginning 2-6 weeks after the last course of R-CHOP, patients who achieve a complete remission (CR) undergo radiotherapy 5 days a week for approximately 5½ weeks.

arms.label: Interventional: 6 R-CHOP-14
arms.text: Arm III (R-CHOP-14): Patients receive R-CHOP as in arm I. Patients also receive filgrastim (G-CSF) subcutaneously once daily on days 4-13 or until blood counts recover. Treatment repeats every 14 days for up to 6 courses in the absence of disease progression or unacceptable toxicity.

arms.label: Interventional: 6 R-CHOP-14 and radiotherapy
arms.text: Arm IV (R-CHOP-14 and radiotherapy): Patients receive R-CHOP as in arm I. Patients also receive G-CSF an in arm III. Treatment repeats every 14 days for up to 6 courses in the absence of disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. Beginning 2-6 weeks after the last course of R-CHOP, patients who achieve CR undergo radiotherapy as in arm II.

arms.label: Arm A (RT, procarbazine, lomustine, vincristine)
arms.text: Patients undergo 3D-CRT or IMRT on days 1-5 for 5-7 weeks. Patients also receive procarbazine hydrochloride PO on days 8-21, lomustine PO on day 1 and vincristine sulfate IV on days 8 and 29 of courses 3-8. Treatment repeats every 6-7 weeks for up to 6 courses in the absence of disease progression or unacceptable toxicity.

arms.label: Arm B (RT, temozolomide)
arms.text: Patients undergo RT as in arm I and receive temozolomide PO QD on days 1-5 for 5-7 weeks. Beginning 4 weeks after completion of concurrent chemoradiotherapy, patients receive adjuvant temozolomide PO QD days 1-5. Treatment with adjuvant temozolomide repeats every 4 weeks for 6-12 courses in the absence of disease progression and unacceptable toxicity.

eligibility: Metastatic disease (stage IV) detected on imaging and histologically and/or cytologically confirmed

NSCLC as per the WHO Classification of Tumours and AJCC 8th Edition TNM Classification, withoutadriver mutation with an actionable first-line targeted therapy, for whom either ICI alone or combination ICI + chemotherapy is indicated.
Oligoprogression on first -line ICI +/ - chemotherapy systemic therapy after at least 3 cycles.
Oligoprogression is evaluated independently for each lesion, and will be defined as follows
Modified Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumours (RECIST 1.1 [Eisenhauer 2009] )

1) At least a 20% increase in the longest diameter (LD) ofalesion except for lymph nodes where only the short axis is measured, taking as reference the smallest LD/short axis recorded since nadir, and ≥ 5 mm increase in the LD/short axis, OR;
2) The appearance of one or more new lesions, each ≥ 5 mm in size. OR
Modified Positron Emission Tomography Response Criteria in Solid Tumours (PERCIST [Wahl 2009] )
1) >30% increase in 18F FDG SUV max, with >0.8 SUV units increase in tumour SUV from previous baseline scan in pattern typical of tumour and not of infection/treatment effect, OR;
2) Visible increase in the extent of 18F-FDG tumour uptake, OR;
3) New 18F-FDG avid lesions typical of cancer (including new bone lesion) and not related to treatment effect and/or infection.

arms.label: Arm A (carboplatin, paclitaxel, radiation therapy)
arms.text: Patients receive carboplatin IV and paclitaxel IV once weekly and undergo radiation therapy QD (Monday-Friday) beginning on day 1 of each cycle. Patients undergo a CT or PET scan during screening and follow-up and undergo collection of blood samples throughout the trial.

arms.label: Arm B (carboplatin, paclitaxel, radiation therapy, nivolumab)
arms.text: Patients receive carboplatin, paclitaxel, and radiation therapy as in Arm A. Patients also receive nivolumab IV over 30 minutes on days 1 and 15 of each cycle. Cycles repeat every week for up to 5 weeks in the absence of disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. Patients undergo a CT or PET scan during screening and follow-up and undergo collection of blood samples throughout the trial.

arms.label: Arm C (nivolumab)
arms.text: Patients receive nivolumab IV over 30 minutes on day 1 of each cycle. Treatment repeats every 4 weeks for up to 13 cycles in the absence of disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. Patients undergo a CT scan and collection of blood samples throughout the trial.

arms.label: Arm D (nivolumab, ipilimumab)
arms.text: Patients receive nivolumab as in Arm C and receive ipilimumab IV over 90 minutes on day 1 of cycles 1 and 4 and day 15 of cycles 2 and 5. arms.label: Group I (fluciclovine PET/CT)
arms.text: Patients for whom initial fluciclovine or PSMA PET/CT does not reveal any abnormalities outside the prostatic fossa undergo PSA rechecks every 3 months, and undergo fluciclovine or PSMA PET/CT once PSA is \> 2 ng/ml. Patients are off study for treatment plan once PSA reaches 10 ng/ml.

arms.label: TN11-1: TNBC patients predicted sensitive to Paclitaxel+Carboplatin+Camrelizumab+Famitinib by AI
arms.text: The TN11 arm explores AI-guided multidisciplinary precision therapy in TNBC. Patients are stratified using an established digital pathology-based AI model that predicts sensitivity to the combination therapy of Paclitaxel, Carboplatin, Camrelizumab and Famitinib. Patients predicted to be sensitive (TN11-1) receive this combination therapy directly.

arms.label: TN11-2: TNBC patients predicted non-sensitive to Paclitaxel+Carboplatin+Camrelizumab+Famitinib by AI
arms.text: TNBC patients predicted to be non-sensitive (TN11-2) to the combination therapy of Paclitaxel, Carboplatin, Camrelizumab and Famitinib first undergo stereotactic body radiation therapy (SBRT). SBRT is delivered to the primary tumor in 3 fractions of 8 Gy (total 24 Gy) over 3-5 days. Following SBRT, patients receive the combination therapy of Paclitaxel, Carboplatin, Camrelizumab and Famitinib.

arms.label: L12
arms.text: Patients with HR+HER2- breast cancer, clinical stage cT1c-4, cN0-3, M0, with either tumor grade ≥2 or Ki-67 ≥20%. Beginning within 3 weeks after initiating brachytherapy, patients receive paclitaxel IV over 3 hours and carboplatin IV over 30-60 minutes on day 1. Chemotherapy repeats every 21 days for up to 3 courses in the absence of disease progression or unacceptable toxicity.

eligibility: HCC with macrovascular invasion: enhancing thrombus with arterial enhancement and washout. Extrahepatic disease is allowed.
At most 5 discrete intrahepatic foci. Sum of diameters under 20 cm. No direct extension into stomach, duodenum, small bowel, or large bowel.
No fibrolamellar, sarcomatoid, or biphenotypic HCC. Child-Pugh A or B7. ECOG 0-2. Age 18 or older.
Pathologic confirmation is strongly recommended. A radiographic AASLD diagnosis is allowed, except when there is a prior or concurrent malignancy, in which case pathology is required.

Prior resection, TACE, or ablation is allowed. No prior systemic therapy or radioembolization for HCC, and no prior liver transplant. No prior radiotherapy that would overlap enough to cause excessive cumulative toxicity.
Step 2 requires confirmation that payment coverage exists for both arms.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Locally advanced unresectable pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma after 4 to 8 months of active chemotherapy, with no radiographic progression and a qualifying CA19-9 response.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Chemotherapy received: mFOLFIRINOX, FOLFIRINOX, or NALIRIFOX versus gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel. If both were used, stratify by the longer regimen, or by the first regimen if the durations were equal.

schema.label: Randomize 1:1

arms.label: Arm 1, standard of care
arms.text: Continue chemotherapy, or 50.4 Gy or 54 Gy in 1.8 Gy fractions with fluoropyrimidine, or observation. Observation is suggested only after 6 months of chemotherapy.

arms.label: Arm 2, dose-escalated RT
arms.text: Default 10 Gy x 5 (BED10 100 Gy). Alternative 3 Gy x 25 (BED10 97.5 Gy). If 5 fractions are not feasible, contact the principal investigator before using 25 fractions.

schema.note: Tumor treating fields are allowed with induction chemotherapy before randomization.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: 3-year overall survival from randomization.

eligibility: Pathologically proven pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, locally advanced and unresectable by NCCN criteria and institutional tumor board review.

4 to 8 months of active chemotherapy with FOLFIRINOX, NALIRIFOX, or gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel. Breaks do not count. A regimen may be switched for toxicity or a CA19-9 that is not declining, not for RECIST progression.
Registration within 45 days of the last day of pre-study chemotherapy.

Restaging after month 4 and before entry shows no progression. If baseline CA19-9 was above 37, the later value is under 200 or has fallen by at least 70%. If baseline CA19-9 was 37 or lower, it must remain 37 or lower.
No overlapping prior radiotherapy. No active duodenal or gastric ulcer and no direct tumor invasion of bowel or stomach. Age 18 or older. ECOG 0-2.

pretreatment.note: AST and ALT at most 3 times the upper limit of normal. If baseline CA19-9 is above 37, concurrent bilirubin is at most 1.5 times the upper limit.

pretreatment.note: CT chest/abdomen/pelvis, CT plus MRI, or PET/CT. Restaging must show at least stable disease.

arms.label: Moderate-Risk Cohort

arms.label: High-Risk Cohort
arms.text: Patients classified as high risk will undergo SCRT, consisting of five fractions of radiation therapy over a two-week period. The study will assess the efficacy, safety, and long-term outcomes of SCRT, including recurrence rates, toxicity profiles, and patient-reported quality of life.

Adequate normal organ and marrow function as defined below (must be done within 30 days prior to enrollment)
platelet count ≥100 x 109/L

The patient must have an ECOG performance status of ≤ 2 (or Karnofsky ≥ 60%).

Must be accessible for treatment and follow-up. Investigators must assure themselves the patients enrolled on this trial will be available for complete documentation of the treatment, adverse events, follow-up and response assessments.
Patients must agree to return to their primary care facility for any adverse events which may occur through the course of the trial.

Pathologic high-risk factors on diagnostic biopsy: high histologic grade (poorly differentiated), mucinous or signet ring histology.

eligibility: Pleasesee Section 4 of the Master EN.10 Protocol, as well as additional sub-study specific criteria described in the EN.10 sub-study sections of the master protocol. Prior to inclusion in this trial, complete molecular classification must be performed on an

EC specimen. This can be either the tumor-containing hysterectomy specimen or the preoperative specimen. Molecular classification includes mutational status assessment of the exonuclease domain of DNA polym erase epsilon ( POLE ), MMR-IHC, estrogen receptor (ER)-IHC, and p53-IHC or TP53 sequencing. The test should be performed in a (pathology) laboratory with accreditation to report clinically validated results by
International Accreditation New Zealand or equivalent. MMR, ER, and p53 IHC testing, and interpretation will be performed locally at each participating center. Centers requiring

POLE sequencing to be performed at another approved site should ship FFPE block, at ambient temperature to that site. Samples sent for testing should consist of the highest viable tumor cells for optimal assay performance. All molecular tests should be completed promptly to ensure patients can be treated or offered active surveillance wit hin 10 weeks of hysterectomy and staging.

Alternatively, the protocol allows flexibility in utilizing different commercial next generation sequencing (NGS) companies to provide services in order to increase the availability of participation in this trial. These companies provide services throughout the country and are not confined to regional or institution type (i.e. academic vs community practice). Molecular classification by NGS is acceptable so long as
HIV-infected patients on effective anti-retroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months are eligible for this trial.

arms.text: Patients receive relugolix PO QD and enzalutamide PO QD on days 1-28 of each cycle. trials.title: OPTimized Dose Escalation With Simultaneous Integrated Boost for High Risk Spinal Metastases: a Prospective Phase II TriAL (OPTIMAL)
trials.population: Spine SBRT is considered a standard of care for the treatment of spinal metastases. Compared to conventional radiation therapy, spine SBRT delivers high doses of radiation to the affected areas to the spinal metastases. This study is interested in seeing whether an additional 'boost' of radiation, delivered to the affected area in the spine, will result in better long-term control of the tumor; help reduce pain; and reduce long-term side effects of radiation therapy.
primary_endpoints: Disease Progression within the Treated Spinal Metastasis, in accordance with SPINO (SPIne assessment in Neuro-Oncology) guidelines

The starting dose and schedule (level 3), as depicted in Figure 2, is the recommended phase II dose and schedule for the combination of adjuvant pembrolizumab, cisplatin, and IMRT for the adjuvant management of pathologic high risk, HPV-negative HNSCC.
Atezolizumab (MPDL3280A, NSC# 783608, IND# 138328)

Atezolizumab isaphage-derived human Ig G1 m Ab against PD-L1. The Fc domain of atezolizumab was engineered to eliminate antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC) or complement-dependent cytotoxicity (CDC) thereby preventing the depletion of T cells expressing
PD-L1 (Lee 2017). Atezolizumab is FDA approved in locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma. Atezolizumab has been evaluated as monotherapy in refractory, recurrent/metastatic

HNSCC and demonstrated an overall response rate of 22%, PFS of 2.6 months, and median OS of 6.0 months, in line with phase I res ults from anti-PD1 m Ab (Colevas 2018). Maintenance atezolizumab after completion of definitive RT for locally advanced HNSCC is now under study inaphase III randomized, placebo-controlled trial (NCT03452137).
Cumulative data from phase I, II, and III studies across multiple solid tumor types indicate that

PD-1 and PD-L1 m Ab are similar in both toxicity profile and clinical activity. The interest of NRG is in adding a PD-1 or PD-L1 m Ab to adjuvant cisplatin-IMRT in high risk, HPV-negative HNSCC; however, we are agnostic as to the specific m Ab.

Given the class toxicity profile of anti-PD1/L1 m Ab, the safety of the combination of atezolizumab, cisplatin, and IMRT in the high-risk adjuvant setting is inferred from NRG HN003. This inference is further supported by phase I data in the definitive setting now available in the public domain, including

Gillison and colleagues reported the results of RTOG Foundation 3504, a multi-arm phase I trial adding nivolumab to definitive RT backbones (Gillison 2018). Nivolumab was safe and feasible to administer concurrently with cisplatin-IMRT, where cisplatin was dosed at 40 mg/m 2 /week or at 100 mg/m 2 every 3 weeks.

Powell and colleagues reported an interim safety analysis including 27 patients onaphase Ib trial of the combination of pembrolizumab 200 mg every 3 weeks, cisplatin 40 mg/m 2/week, and IMRT in the definitive setting for locally advanced HNSCC (Powell 2016). The immune- related toxicity rate in these 27 patients was no different from pembrolizumab monotherapy, and the regimen was both tolerable and feasible.
1. 5 Importance of This Trial ( 20-MAR-2020 )

Initial Design: The proposed randomized phase II-III trial will address several important issues in head and neck cancer. Approximately 50% of head and neck cancer patients undergo primary surgery for their malignancy. For those with high-risk clinical and pathologic features ( eg bone destruction, extracapsular nodal extension, tumor involving resection margins) [Peters 1993; Ang

2001; Bernier 2005), the local-regional failure rates remain high and efforts to reduce recurrence include the use of postoperati ve radiation, and more recently, postoperative chemoradiation. The beneficial impact of adding cisplatin chemotherapy to radiation in the high-risk setting is modest and is accompanied by significant incremental toxicity (including ototoxicity, nephrotoxicity, neutropenia, nausea, and

This study will therefore address the question whether docetaxel alone is as active as docetaxel and cetuximab combination and whether either taxane-based regimen is better than cisplatin monotherapy given to this high-risk group of patients with concurrent radiation. The less toxic weekly cisplatin regimen is selected to enhance compliance in the control arm and to parallel to weekly regimen proposed for the 2

Merged Design: The amended phase III design addsthe NRG-HN003 regimen (cisplatin-IM RT + anti-PD1 or PDL1 m Ab) asathird arm to RTOG 1216 when it re-opens to Phase III. Fromadrug development standpoint, the major goal is to telescope the development of an anti-PD1/PDL1 m Ab in the high-risk adjuvant space. This recommendation stems from the 2014 NCI/CTEP and
HN Steering Committee’s Clinical Trials Planning Meeting, entitled Immunotherapy of Head and

Neck Cancer (Bauman 2017). Given the poor overall outcomes for this curative-intent patient population, and the groundbreaking outcomes for anti-PD1 immunotherapy in the recurrent/ metastatic setting, this was recommended asahigh priority.
In order to efficiently address the immunotherapy question in this patient population, a new phase
III comparison of adjuvant CRT +/-atezo lizumab is being added to the phase III component of
RTOG 1216 asamajor amendment. The merged phase III design has the following advantages

1) Significant head start. Allowsaphase III trial evaluating theaddition of a PD1 or PDL1 m Ab to cisplatin-IMRT in the high-risk adjuvant space to start in 2019. Whereas, serial phase III designs would require deferring trial start until at least 2023.
2) Design efficiency. Leverages the use ofacommon control arm (cisplatin-IMRT) dur ing the period of joint accrual.

3) Two independent phase III comparisons. Two primary phase III comparisons of OS will be conducted: a) cisplatin-IMRT vs. docetaxel-cetuximab-IMRT; b) cisplatin-IMRT vs. atezolizumab plus cisplatin-IMRT.

By the use of this efficient merged design, both human and fiscal resources are appropriately governed within the NCTN portfolio. There is no competing trial in the adjuvant, high risk space within the NCTN or industry.
